requestedIntent: Owner decision 2026-10-27: one model-choice rule for Claude and Codex agents in every host. A work-class table (critical, standard, mechanical, light, browser tour, trivial lookup) with the Claude model and the Codex model/effort for each, an effort section (four questions, levels, one-level escalation, no double payment), precedence of a project's recorded decision, waiting rules (background jobs, hand-off before long waits or past ~300k context, no watcher model), and an acef-note logging rule; the BMAD routing policy mapping follows the same table.
limitations: Wired, not enforced: nothing stops an ordinary Claude Code subagent or Codex run from using a higher class or effort than the table gives. Only actors admitted through ACEF routing (Full roles, Fix/Standard dispatches under admitted-role-routing-v1) are checked by the hard-wall hook, and they follow the routing policy, not the table.
Claude Code subagent effort comes from the agent definition frontmatter; ACEF ships no agent definitions per class, so the Claude effort levels apply only where a host defines them.
The gpt-6.1-sol mapping is carried over from the V327-CAL-001 calibration of gpt-5.6-sol without recalibration.

The routing policy has three execution classes and its anthropic mapping is Sonnet for every class (owner decision 2026-10-27). Development cannot run on Sonnet with an Opus review inside the policy: Patch Assurance and both Judges share semantic-critical with Development. A host that wants Opus review dispatches it through its own process.
Effect not measured: no host has recorded model and effort per report yet, so the weekly retro has no effort comparison.

evidence.note: 2026-10-27: openai roles resolve to gpt-6.1-sol; every anthropic role resolves to claude-sonnet-5-5; policy note names MODEL_CHOICE.md.
